scope_note: Decision-relevant modeled syntheses for Apple Mesa and Switch Citadel / Tahoe Reno 1. These values are derived from cited public evidence and explicit assumptions; they are not observed, audited, source-reported, or causal unless a record explicitly says otherwise. They remain outside canonical claims and source-record counts.

sources.title: Foreign-Trade Zones Board Annual Report to Congress, 2024
sources.notes: The Mesa FTZ 221 table reports 101–150 employees across all activated zone activity and reports Apple production exports in a $75–100 million band. The employee band is not Apple-only.

sources.title: FTZ Annual Report Tips
sources.notes: Defines reported FTZ employment as direct and contract employees within the activated area, with part-time workers stated as full-time equivalents.

sources.title: 2023 County Business Patterns: Maricopa County, NAICS 518210
sources.notes: County industry benchmark: 12,467 March employees and $1,182,395,000 annual payroll for computing $94,841.98 payroll per employee. Both employment and payroll carry the Census H noise flag.

sources.title: Data Center Air Management Tool User's Manual v3.1
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
sources.notes: Defines onsite WUE as annual onsite water divided by annual IT-equipment energy and gives an approximately 2 L/kWh U.S. average data-center WUE reference point.

sources.title: The environmental footprint of data centers in the United States
sources.notes: Provides state-of-the-art annualized PUE 1.17 and WUE 0.55 L/kWh benchmark inputs used for the low-water scenario.

sources.title: Historical Arizona Assessment Ratios
sources.notes: Reports Class 1 assessment ratios of 17% in 2023, 16.5% in 2024, and 16% in 2025, compared with the 5% Class 6 FTZ ratio.

sources.title: Foreign-Trade Zone Duty Savings Estimator
sources.notes: Describes FTZ duty-savings mechanisms. Public Apple Mesa records do not disclose HTS mix, foreign-status share, or effective duty rates, so the modeled export component is an assumption-driven sensitivity only.

sources.title: Foreign-Trade Zone 221 zone details
sources.notes: The current official zone profile reports 85.67 activated acres in FTZ 221. Acreage is used only as an explicit allocation key, not as evidence that employment is spatially proportional.

sources.title: Foreign-Trade Zone 221, Subzone 00A details
sources.notes: The current official subzone profile identifies Apple Inc. as the active operator of 83.17 activated acres at 3740 S. Signal Butte Road.

sources.title: Electric Power Annual, Table 2.10: Average Price of Electricity to Ultimate Customers by End-Use Sector, by State, 2024 and 2023
sources.notes: Reports 2024 Arizona average retail prices of 7.90 cents per kWh for industrial customers and 12.23 cents per kWh for commercial customers. These are statewide sector averages, not Apple's SRP tariff or bill.

sources.title: eGRID2023 Revision 2 summary data
sources.notes: Reports an AZNM subregion annual total-output emission rate of 706.189 pounds CO2e per MWh. The rate supports a location-based gross-emissions benchmark, not Apple's market-based inventory.

sources.title: Apple Environmental Progress Report 2025
sources.notes: Reports that a pilot resin-treatment system reduced makeup-water use by 30 percent and was being implemented at Mesa. It does not report completion, Mesa applicability, or measured Mesa savings.

sources.title: Avoiding Waste Heat through AI Infrastructure Thermal Integration
sources.notes: Reports an industry-average data-center PUE of approximately 1.4 in 2023. The value is used only as a conservative sensitivity bound, not as a Tahoe Reno 1 observation.

sources.title: Tesla Expansion Economic Impact Analysis
sources.publisher: Nevada Governor's Office of Economic Development
sources.notes: Public same-region IMPLAN analysis reports $1.6 billion of direct industrial-construction spending, 9,275 direct person-year jobs, and $924.023 million of direct labor income for 2023-2027 in Washoe and Storey Counties. Its asset mix, scale, timing and contractor mix differ from Citadel; the transfer is therefore sensitivity-tested and used only for direct construction channels. The report combines indirect and induced channels, so those channels are not transferred.

sources.title: Nevada Data Center Abatements
sources.publisher: Nevada Governor's Office of Economic Development
sources.notes: Current public program summary states that data-center applicants must ensure at least 50% of construction workers are Nevada residents. This is a compliance threshold, not an observation of Switch worker residence, hours, payroll or supplier location.

sources.title: Switch February 2019 Investor Presentation
sources.publisher: Switch, Inc. / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
sources.notes: The filed presentation reports Tahoe Reno 1 opened in 2016, 1.36 million gross square feet, up to 130 MW delivered power at full build-out, 30% utilization by available data-center space and 58% utilization by available cabinets/power capacity for the 2018 operating snapshot. Capacity and utilization are not meter readings.

sources.title: Tahoe Reno 02 Citadel Campus One-Sheet
sources.notes: Operator marketing reports 100% renewable campus power, more than 3,300 acre-feet of effluent-water availability, and 1.18 PUE for one sector. The PUE is a benchmark bound only; it is not a Tahoe Reno 1 whole-building annual measurement. Water availability is not consumption.

sources.title: eGRID2023 Summary Tables, Nevada State Output Emission Rate
sources.notes: eGRID2023 reports a Nevada total-output rate of 642.7 lb CO2e/MWh. The statewide 2023 generation-average factor is used for a location-based scenario and does not measure Citadel's supplier, contract instruments, hourly marginal emissions or market-based Scope 2 result.

sources.title: BLS QCEW annual averages, Storey County total covered employment, 2011-2019
sources.notes: Study panel values use annual QCEW total covered employment for Storey County (FIPS 32029): 3,090, 3,424, 3,893 and 4,797 in 2011-2014; 11,105, 17,199 and 17,997 in 2017-2019. The series covers all employers and is strongly confounded by Tesla and broader Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center growth.
